institution: Bharati Vidyapeeth (Deemed to be University) Medical College and Hospital, Pune
period: Year 2022 (printed as "isolate listing and antibiogram for the year 2022"; months not stated, read as the calendar year)
citation: Bharati Vidyapeeth (Deemed to be University) Medical College Hospital and Research Centre, Pune. Antimicrobial Policy and Antimicrobial Stewardship Program 2023-2024, Version 9.0 (released 28.03.2023), section 5: organisms commonly isolated and antibiogram, area wise, for the year 2022, pp. 10 to 37. Pune: Bharati Hospital; 2023.
reporting: Percent susceptible (whole numbers) by organism and specimen within each area (ICU, ward departments, OPD), with the number of patients per organism row; Candida tables with antifungals; pie charts of the top isolates by specimen with data labels. Colour bands mark usefulness; grey cells are not tested. No hospital-wide table.
method: Not stated in the report (no AST method, breakpoint standard or duplicate-isolate rule given).

verification.note: ICU tables (pp11 to 12) and OPD tables (pp35 to 36) were parsed from the PDF text layer by character position (each number assigned to the nearest rotated column header and to its row by the Number of patients cell), then compared value by value, all cells and all n, against the pages rendered at scale 3.5 and cropped into column groups. Specimen groups were read from the rendered pages. Pie-chart counts (p10 ICU, p34 OPD) were read from the embedded chart images upscaled 3x: each data label was assigned to its slice by colour and by the legend order (slices run clockwise from 12 o'clock in legend order), and the larger slices were checked against their label boxes. The OPD urine pie gives its small slices as callouts; their assignment was confirmed by measuring the slice angles (P. aeruginosa 32 vs E. faecalis 28, S. aureus 14, E. faecium 12, E. cloacae 10).

notes: Area-wise antibiogram section (pages 10 to 37) of the Bharati Hospital Pune antimicrobial policy version 9.0 (2023-2024), with data for 2022. The report has no hospital-wide table. Rows kept: the ICU Gram-negative, Gram-positive and Candida tables (pp11 to 12) and the OPD Gram-negative and Gram-positive tables (pp35 to 36). OPD blood isolates come from Emergency Department cultures (p34); the OPD tables have no blood rows. Ward departments (Medicine, Surgery, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Orthopaedics, Oncology), the NICU and the combined Paediatrics and PICU section have their own tables only, with no combined ward table, so they are listed in excluded; the report does not say whether its ICU tables cover all adult ICUs. Because no ward rows exist, a combination of the OPD and ICU rows is not a hospital-wide figure. n is the printed "Number of patients"; the report warns that most organisms have fewer than 30 isolates. Counts are the data labels of the top-isolate pie charts (ICU blood, pus, sputum and urine on p10; OPD blood, pus, sputum and urine on p34) for charted organisms with a keyed, unambiguous name. Several chart counts are 1 to 4 higher than the table n of the same organism (listed in the row notes); the charts may count isolates and the tables patients. Specimen totals printed beside the charts: ICU blood 611, pus 134, sputum 96, urine 215; OPD blood 86, pus 374, sputum 14, urine 664. The ICU blood coagulase-negative staphylococci rows are the isolates the report lists as skin flora or collection contamination (p11). Likewise the OPD blood chart counts of S. epidermidis (8) and S. haemolyticus (5) are the isolates the report lists as skin flora or collection contamination in the EMD (p34: S. epidermidis 8, S. haemolyticus 5, Micrococcus luteus 3).

issues: Second reader 2026-09-26: all 560 cells, all 43 row n and all 65 chart counts re-read from the page images and written down before comparing with the file (tables rendered at scale 4 to 5 and cropped by column group; pie charts from the embedded chart images upscaled 3x). This covers the seeded 25% sample (140 cells over all five tables). 0 errors, nothing corrected; organism, specimen group and setting (ICU pp11 to 12, OPD pp35 to 36) agree for every row.

Second reader: the 19 cells the validator does not keep (8 fosfomycin cautions, 4 intrinsic, 7 hidden) are printed as recorded, e.g. ICU blood B. cepacia amikacin 0 and gentamicin 0, E. cloacae amoxicillin-clavulanate 0 in ICU blood and OPD urine.

Second reader: the 10 count mismatches are printed that way, chart label above table n in every case: ICU blood K. pneumoniae 65 vs 64, E. coli 45 vs 44, A. baumannii 45 vs 43, B. cepacia 25 vs 23, S. aureus 31 vs 30, E. faecium 23 vs 22; OPD pus P. aeruginosa 59 vs 56, E. coli 50 vs 49; OPD urine E. coli 396 vs 392, K. pneumoniae 101 vs 100. No chart count is below its table n. The charts sit beside specimen totals headed "No of isolates" and the tables print "Number of patients"; the ICU blood contamination list gives as isolates the same CoNS numbers (70, 48, 33, 19, 11) that the Gram-positive table gives as patients. This fits charts counting isolates and tables counting patients, but the report states no duplicate rule, so the row notes rightly say "may".

Second reader: chart slices without inside labels were checked by measuring slice boundary angles. OPD urine: P. aeruginosa 32 and E. faecalis 28 confirmed (grey slice about 18 degrees, gold about 16; 32 and 28 of 612 give 18.8 and 16.5), E. faecium 12, E. cloacae 10, P. mirabilis 8 and S. aureus 14 also fit; A. baumannii 5 against K. pneumoniae ozaenae 6 cannot be told apart reliably (two slices of about 3 degrees; the widths weakly favour the recorded 5). OPD pus: E. cloacae 8, M. morganii 6, P. mirabilis 11, E. faecalis 5 confirmed.
Second reader: added one sentence to notes: the OPD blood chart counts of S. epidermidis 8 and S. haemolyticus 5 are the EMD contamination isolates listed on p34.
